Parking it. Parking moves the unticked stage and every Ranked-list item into the deferred backlog, then retires the roadmap. Here are the steps, written as tool calls.

**1. Read the item schema and the current backlog, and get the date**

```
Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/references/deferred-backlog.md
Read specs/deferred_items.md        # may not exist yet
Bash: date +%F
Bash: ls specs/ specs/completed/ 2>/dev/null
```

The `ls` checks for methodology or critique files to retire alongside. With no spec behind this roadmap, I expect none.

**2. Append to `specs/deferred_items.md`**

This adds one section, `## lock-closures-roadmap — <date>`, with four items. Each follows the schema from step 1 and stands on its own, carrying Stage 1's result (closures under 2% of days below 3.1 m, rising to about 60% at 3.8 m; one fit on 1.8 GB took 22 minutes on a laptop):

| Item | Size (from the roadmap's cost note) | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| Stage 2: closure notices (O5, Track B) | small: one closure-log poll every 10 minutes | the notice job and its operator mailing list exist, and in a test an email reaches every address within an hour of a new closure entry |
| O2: 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock | small: one model run a day on Stage 1's model | a 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock comes from the river-level forecast |
| O3: pooled per-lock curves for all 14 locks | about 14× Stage 1's data (roughly 25 GB) | separate closure curves for all 14 locks, pooled across locks |
| O4: closure-history map for boat operators | about a day of work | a closure-history map page is available to the canal's boat operators |

**3. Retire the roadmap**

```
Bash: mkdir -p specs/completed && git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
Edit specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md: add under the title
      PARKED (<date>) — 1 of 2 stages complete
Bash: git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
Bash: git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap: funding ended; Stage 2 and Track A ranked list moved to deferred_items"
```

Stage 1's findings file and plan 4 stay where they are, as the record of what was done.

When these have run, I'll report the commit and anything that differed from the above. That includes any schema field in the deferred-backlog reference that the table doesn't cover.

One note: Track B was split off because operator notices are useful whether or not the curve holds. If those notices are funded separately, you can promote Stage 2 back out of `deferred_items.md` on its own. As you asked, it's parked with the rest.
